requirements.quote: Endpoints need to eventually agree on the amount of flow control credit that has been consumed on every stream, to be able to account for all bytes for connection-level flow control.
requirements.condition: For every stream whose bytes contribute to connection-level flow control accounting.
requirements.required_behavior: Endpoints eventually agree on the amount of flow-control credit consumed on the stream and account for all bytes at the connection level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Endpoints must not leave per-stream consumed credit permanently inconsistent or omit stream bytes from connection-level flow-control accounting.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can compare the peers' eventual consumed-credit accounting for each stream and verify that all stream bytes are included in connection-level accounting.

requirements.quote: On receipt of a RESET_STREAM frame, an endpoint will tear down state for the matching stream and ignore further data arriving on that stream.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a RESET_STREAM frame for a matching stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint tears down state for the matching stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not retain the stream's operational state after processing the reset.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream state can be inspected after RESET_STREAM processing to verify that the matching stream was torn down.

requirements.quote: On receipt of a RESET_STREAM frame, an endpoint will tear down state for the matching stream and ignore further data arriving on that stream.
requirements.condition: Data arrives on a stream after the endpoint has received a RESET_STREAM frame for that stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint ignores the further arriving data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not deliver or otherwise process further arriving data as stream data.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can inject stream data after RESET_STREAM and verify that it is neither delivered nor processed.

requirements.quote: RESET_STREAM terminates one direction of a stream abruptly.
requirements.condition: A RESET_STREAM frame is applied to a stream direction.
requirements.required_behavior: The affected direction enters an abruptly terminated state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The RESET_STREAM must not terminate more than the affected stream direction.
requirements.why_checkable: The state transition of the affected stream direction can be observed after processing RESET_STREAM.

requirements.quote: For a bidirectional stream, RESET_STREAM has no effect on data flow in the opposite direction.
requirements.condition: RESET_STREAM terminates one direction of a bidirectional stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Data flow in the opposite direction remains unaffected.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not stop, reset, or otherwise alter opposite-direction data flow solely because RESET_STREAM was applied to the other direction.
requirements.why_checkable: A bidirectional-stream test can reset one direction and verify that data continues to flow normally in the opposite direction.

requirements.quote: Both endpoints MUST maintain flow control state for the stream in the unterminated direction until that direction enters a terminal state.
requirements.condition: One direction of a bidirectional stream has been terminated by RESET_STREAM while the opposite direction has not entered a terminal state.
requirements.required_behavior: Both endpoints maintain flow-control state for the stream in the unterminated direction until that direction enters a terminal state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Neither endpoint may discard the unterminated direction's flow-control state before that direction enters a terminal state.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can reset one direction and inspect flow-control tracking throughout the opposite direction's lifetime, including its transition to a terminal state.
